title: The NYU Faculty Strike and the Politics of Workers’ Rights
author: Dan Falcone
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Screen-
Shot-2026-03-24-at-7.38.35-PM-680x483.png)

Image by Richard Lu.

Just days ago, NYU faced an [imminent faculty
strike](https://www.amny.com/education/nyu-strike-imminent-negotiations-
continue/) of nearly 1,000 non-tenure track faculty as questions about labor
conditions and university governance come into focus. In this exclusive
interview for _CounterPunch_ , [Professor Rebecca
Karl](https://as.nyu.edu/faculty/rebecca-
karl.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1), a historian
specializing in Modern Chinese History, provides insight into the political
factors fueling the dispute. The university’s shift toward contract and
adjunct faculty is raising concerns over [job
security](https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/nyu-faculty-monday-strike-
deadline/) and academic freedom. Now that the
[strike](https://www.nydailynews.com/2026/03/23/nyu-professors-go-on-strike-
for-raises-job-security-classes-continue/) has come to fruition, Karl breaks
down trends in higher education and highlights the barriers faced by NYU
workers throughout the city, country and world**.**

**Daniel Falcone:** According to an article by Natalie Deoragh in [
_Washington Square News,_ ](https://nyunews.com/2026/02/28/contract-faculty-
set-strike-deadline-for-march-23)NYU’s contract faculty union planned to
strike if no agreement was reached by [March
23](https://www.amny.com/news/nyu-professors-on-strike-at-manhattan-school/).
What were the main issues driving the possibility of
[strike](https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/nyu-faculty-strike-deadline/),
and how do you think it shows how higher‑ed labor relations and political
power are playing out in universities?

**Rebecca Karl:** One of the main driving
[issues](https://www.nyu.edu/about/news-publications/contract-faculty-union-
negotiations/the-facts.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1) is
how NYU in the last few decades has restructured its
[faculty](https://nyucontractfacultyunion.org/information-for-the-nyu-
community/) in fundamental ways; this transformation is not unique to NYU, but
NYU has done this at greater speed and with more intention than most. The
previous reliance on [tenured/tenure-track
faculty](https://www.aaup.org/tenure) lines has been completely eviscerated in
large parts of the university and unevenly across the whole university, in
favor of the lower-paid and less secure alternative of contract and adjunct
faculty labor. Most of these faculty -- aside from the professionals who come
in as practitioners -- have the same degrees, the same training, the same
commitments to research and teaching as those of us on tenured lines, which
are job-secured and carry benefits.

Because of overall restructuring of universities and defunding nationally, the
only jobs available are [contingent ones](https://www.oracle.com/human-
capital-management/workforce-management/what-is-contingent-workforce/).
Contract and [adjunct faculty](https://www.aft.org/news/new-aft-report-
adjunct-faculty-remain-underpaid-underappreciated) are hired as second-class
citizens. Contingency works to keep labor in perpetual fear of losing jobs,
especially when individual contract negotiations upon
[renewal](https://www.etui.org/sites/default/files/2024-09/Experimenting%20for%20union%20renewal-
challenges%2C%20illustrations%20and%20lessons_2024_0.pdf) are left to the
vagaries of vindictive deans and/or administrations looking to yet again cut
costs on the backs of faculty and teaching (while jacking up and maintaining
their own sky-high salaries and benefits).

What the [union](https://nyucontractfacultyunion.org/information-for-the-nyu-
community/) is organized around and negotiating for are thus: more predictable
renewals based in [peer review](https://msutoday.msu.edu/news/2025/09/ask-the-
expert-peer-review) not [administrative
logic](https://www.wisdomlib.org/concept/administrative-logic); salaries that
are commensurate to the work rendered and the importance of contract faculty
in the institution (now over 50% of the teaching faculty at the university);
guarantees about academic [freedom and
protection](https://www.aaup.org/academe/issues/winter-2021/do-adjuncts-have-
academic-freedom-or-why-tenure-matters) from political targeting; defense
against being rendered redundant by AI modules; among others. These are issues
indicative of more general assaults on higher education by political, tech,
and financial authorities, to which NYU’s administration, led by President
[Linda Mills](https://www.nyu.edu/about/leadership-university-
administration/organization-directory/office-of-the-
president/biography.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1) and
Provost [Gigi Dopico](https://as.nyu.edu/faculty/georgina-
dopico.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1), has capitulated
and usually pre-emptively prostrated itself in shameful fashion.

**Daniel Falcone:** Amita Chatterjee in [ _The Chronicle of Higher
Education_](https://www.chronicle.com/article/adjunct-professors-face-a-
constant-struggle-to-not-give-up-report-says) described how contingent and
adjunct faculty were facing [uncertainty](https://nationalpress.org/topic/how-
job-uncertainty-affects-mental-health/), limited job security, and challenging
work conditions. Do you see structural issues playing into the NYU contract
faculty’s [fight](https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2026/03/nyc-
electeds-back-nyu-faculty-union-strike-looming/412262/) for a [first
contract](https://www.leftvoice.org/solidarity-with-the-nyu-contract-faculty-
strike/)?

**Rebecca Karl:** Yes, restructuring higher education, and at
[NYU](https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/video/nyu-students-join-faculty-on-
strike-saying-they-are-willing-to-stand-for-whats-right/), is hugely
responsible for this situation. NYU decided some [decades
ago](https://www.socialistworker.org/2005-2/568/568_11_NYU.php) (under [John
Sexton](https://its.law.nyu.edu/facultyprofiles/index.cfm?fuseaction=profile.biography&personid=20281))
to pivot towards contract faculty away from tenure lines as part of its
[imperial growth](https://www.nyu.edu/academics/studying-abroad.html) around
the world and in Greenwich Village/ Brooklyn; it is reaping what it sowed
(See: “[NYU Eats World](https://www.chronicle.com/article/nyu-eats-world/)”).
Contract faculty at the New York campus are hugely united behind the union and
behind the necessity to strike, if forced by NYU’s intransigence.

The adjunct union and the non-unionized tenured faculty are strongly in
solidarity with contract faculty, and many of us have pledged to refuse to do
[struck work](https://www.lawinsider.com/clause/struck-work), even though the
university is encouraging scab labor from all its units and resources –
including, reportedly, from [Abu Dhabi](https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/), [Tel
Aviv](https://www.nyu.edu/telaviv.html),
[Shanghai](https://shanghai.nyu.edu/), and other places. The lengths to which
this administration will go to break the union are astonishing, although of
course not surprising. The university has always been hugely anti-union and
has expended phenomenal amounts of money on [law
firms](https://prospect.org/2025/09/01/2025-09-01-anti-union-law-firm-illegal-
captive-audience-littler-mendelson-rhode-island/) aiming to break unions, not
successfully but at great cost.

**Daniel Falcone:** In an article by [ _The American Prospect_
](https://prospect.org/2026/02/25/nyu-professors-vote-to-strike-uaw-trump-
labor-nlrb/)on the months of bargaining with management, Whitney Curry Wimbish
contextualizes it with national classroom labor struggles. Is the NYU matter a
local dispute, or part of a bigger capitalistic struggle?

**Rebecca Karl:** This is a much bigger struggle that is playing out in
microcosm at the university level. [Casualization of
labor](https://anticapitalistresistance.org/fighting-casualisation-and-job-
insecurity/) is universally practiced now, less in the breach, more as a norm
across the board. Unionization of academic labor across public and private
universities is one of the bright spots in the labor movement today in the
U.S.

**Daniel Falcone:** According to Sara Wexler of [
_Jacobin_](https://jacobin.com/2026/02/nyu-full-time-contingent-faculty-
strike), in talking with [Brendan
Hogan](https://liberalstudies.nyu.edu/about/faculty-listing/brendan-
hogan.html), Elisabeth Fay, and [Fanny Shum](https://jacobin.com/author/fanny-
shum), NYU’s contract faculty union planned to
[strike](https://www.amny.com/news/nyu-strike-students-back-faculty-contract-
talks/) if no agreement was reached. Since their conversation in February,
described as pulling “[the emergency
brake](https://x.com/jasonhickel/status/1334795290373722112?s=20) on the
process of casualization” and centering on “job security” and fair pay -- can
you provide an update on how negotiations have progressed of late and comment
on your expectations for post [March
23](https://nyucontractfacultyunion.org/information-for-the-nyu-community/)
life at NYU?

**Rebecca Karl:** I know the pace of negotiation is quickening, but I’m not in
the room, as are [Elisabeth Fay](https://x.com/schadenfreulein) and the
others. I expect, if the strike is forced by NYU intransigence, that the
administration will be doing its utmost to pretend that things are going on as
usual and that serving our students is the primary goal in their increasingly
disturbed rhetoric.

If serving our [students](https://yaledailynews.com/articles/nyu-grad-
students-move-toward-unionization) were in fact what they cared about, they’d
care about the conditions of student learning, which requires paying the
professors who teach them a living wage and protecting them from the worst of
contingency -- the threat of the sudden loss of a job and of livelihood. I
imagine that certain programs will be affected far more than others, since
contract faculty are not evenly spread through the university. I imagine that
the university will attempt to find
[scabs](https://nyucontractfacultyunion.org/information-for-the-nyu-
community/) off the street if necessary [to cover
classes](https://x.com/yuhline/status/2033325709167350154?s=20) (I heard one
story that they suggested going to immigrant communities to find native
speakers of a language to come into the classroom to replace professional
language teachers!).

I imagine that undergraduate [students](https://www.amny.com/news/nyu-strike-
students-back-faculty-contract-talks/) -- many of whom have been [mobilized in
support](https://www.instagram.com/p/DV_WzjejWR4/) -- will be vocally out on
the [picket lines](https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/video/nyu-students-join-
faculty-on-strike-saying-they-are-willing-to-stand-for-whats-right/); I
imagine that the graduate students, who are
[unionized](https://makingabetternyu.org/), will be picketing too. And I
imagine the administration will hype up their divisive rhetoric and I imagine
that we -- one faculty united in solidarity -- will fight back relentlessly.

**Daniel Falcone:** Now that the
[strike](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DWPOE5piZSi/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link)
has commenced, would you like to add any additional commentary related to the
dispute?

**Rebecca Karl:** From what I’ve seen in pictures and descriptions, it is huge
and comprised not only of [CFU members](https://abc7ny.com/post/tenured-
faculty-members-represented-cfu-uaw-nyu-go-strike/18755836/) on strike, but
adjuncts, undergraduate students and grad students, as well as sympathetic
local unions. We’re hoping the numbers remain strong and the university is
crippled. The central administration has predictably offered ridiculous
bromide messaging that “[strikes are
disruptive](https://www.nyu.edu/about/news-publications/news/2026/march/new-
research.html)” and “[we’re negotiating in good
faith](https://www.nyu.edu/about/news-
publications/news/2026/january/J.html?challenge=d06e90d7-4d8f-4b88-9d8c-10b73beb60f1).”

Obviously strikes are intentionally disruptive; that’s their purpose as a
last-resort tool of labor against employers. They have not been negotiating in
good faith, and meanwhile they’ve been strong-arming staff, administrators,
and wavering faculty of all ranks into doing struck work.

Finally, though, I find it unconscionable that our administration would add to
everyone’s anxieties and sense of foreboding -- due to
[ICE](https://www.aacu.org/liberaleducation/articles/ice-on-campus-what-to-do)
at our airports and on our streets, disrupted travel and student distress over
visas and classes, war across the world, an erratic insane
[president](https://www.npr.org/2025/05/30/nx-s1-5415678/president-trumps-war-
on-higher-education) who [destroys
countries](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_8T_rKnQPFk) and murders untold
numbers of people he dislikes.

In such a situation of intense unease among all of us, that NYU’s
“[leadership](https://www.nyu.edu/about/leadership-university-
administration.html)” would add to all this by refusing to pay a [living
wage](https://www.thecity.nyc/2026/03/23/nyu-faculty-strike-wages/) to its
faculty, by denying folks who work hard for a living some sense of security
for their livelihoods, by insulting our intelligence and treating students
like [disposable consumers](https://truthout.org/articles/we-will-not-be-your-
disposable-labor-graduate-student-workers-fight-for-economic-rights-goes-
beyond-the-gop-assault/)…is just appalling to me. It demonstrates how craven
NYU has become and how little the institution values education and educators.

Rights](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/03/25/the-nyu-faculty-strike-and-
the-politics-of-workers-rights/) appeared first on
[CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
